A muscle fibre relaxes when its motor neuron stops firing, so acetylcholine is cleared from the neuromuscular junction and the fibre stops being excited. Calcium is then actively pumped back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum by SERCA, which lets tropomyosin re-block the myosin-binding sites on actin. The question is cut off after "when:", so I've assumed it asks for the standard textbook condition.
